al_roof_rock.blurb: Roof Rock is a small boulder cluster inside Hurricane Creek Park in Tuscaloosa, reached by a riverside trail from the lot. The main rock is a tall face with pockets leading to a crack beneath a short overhanging roof. There are six problems, all easy to moderate: a couple at the very bottom of the scale, several around V0, one V1 and a V2 at the top end. That makes it a gentle stop for beginners, kids or a warm-up session rather than a destination for hard climbers. Expect a low, creekside setting close to the university, with other rocks further along the cliff line.

al_ripple_effect_boulder.blurb: Ripple Effect Boulder is the headline block at Sauta Cave, a small bouldering zone on the west flank of Pine Mountain in northeast Alabama. It holds six problems, running from mid-range V3 and V4 up through a V6 and two problems near V9, so it suits stronger boulderers more than novices. The signature line heads straight up the main face, and a few easier problems give a way to warm up. The walk in is rough: the old path has grown over, so plan on pushing through brush and following the gully uphill.

al_arecibo_boulders.blurb: Arecibo Boulders is a compact group on Bishop Mountain, in the Middle Bishop cluster near Huntsville. The centerpiece is a dish-shaped block with a second boulder tucked beneath it; the problems work the lip of the roof and the pit below. The handful of lines span roughly V2 to V6, with the hardest being the steepest roof problem, so it fits climbers already comfortable on moderate boulders. The blocks sit near the edge of TVA land, so stay close to the road. Reaching them means walking along the top of the cliff and then cutting back to the right.

al_anarchy_boulders.blurb: Anarchy Boulders is a pair of blocks within Moss Rock Preserve in Hoover, outside Birmingham. The big boulder carries a painted-looking letter A, which gives the spot its name. Problems are short and friendly, mostly V0 with a few at V1 or V2, so this is a good corner for newer boulderers and for easing into a session. Few people come here, so some of the hollow-sounding holds may be fragile; test them before committing. Walk past the Lost Roof Boulder and up a small rise to reach it from the preserve's main boulder field.

al_nuclear_arms_boulder.blurb: Nuclear Arms Boulder is a tall block right beside the road at The Citadel, a roadside boulderfield near Fort Payne. It is the first major boulder you meet heading south from the lot, to the right of the map kiosk, so the walk is almost nothing. Six problems range from about V2 to V6, mostly in the V3 to V4 band, with shouldery moves and sandy landings that earned it a nickname among locals. This was the first section of The Citadel to see development, and it makes an easy early stop before exploring the rest of the field.
